Special Population Groups 
 
* Paediatric: may present with more non-specific or atypical symptoms. 
* Pregnancy: due to displacement of the uterus, presentation may be atypical. 
A leukocytosis in pregnancy is normal. 
* Elderly: do not mount the usual inflammatory response. The usual signs & symptoms 
of appendicitis may be reduced, atypical or even absent. Tend to present later. 
* Immunocompromised: do not mount the usual inflammatory response. 

Contents 
 
 
ACUTE CHOLECYSTITIS 
 
 
 
CLINICAL FEATURES 
Symptoms 
*RUQ pain / epigastric pain 
*Nausea 
*Vomiting 
*Anorexia 
*Low grade fever 
Signs 
*Vital signs parallel the degree of illness 
*± Jaundice 
*Epigastric / RUQ tenderness 
*Abdominal guarding 
*Murphy’s sign 
➔ inspiratory pause on palpation of RUQ 
*Search for complications & other sources of 
pain 
 
 
 
 
RISK FACTORS 
*Increasing age 
*Female 
*Parity 
*Family history 
*Obesity 
*Diabetes Mellitus 
*Profound weight loss 
*Fasting 
*Cystic fibrosis 
*Malabsorption syndromes 
*Medications e.g. antibiotics, lipid lowering, 
diuretics, oestrogen-containing, steroids 
 
ED MANAGEMENT 
The primary goal of ED care is resuscitation, stabilization and an 
expedient diagnosis 
RESUSCITATION 
*ABC approach 
*IV line – 20mls/kg Balsol/Ringer’s Lactate fluid bolus if shocked 
INVESTIGATIONS 
*Beds
